title: A helper file is named by its record: the code standard counts it as the record's file for R05 and R01, and not for R02
when: Reads a spec built for the test whose helper_file table names helper files of a predicate record, one in the package of the record's file and one in a package that a record of another domain names, through ReadSpec. Then it runs assure.fileWithoutRecord, assure.packageOfTwoDomains and assure.identifierMissing over a tree built for it. Then it reads the same spec without the helper_file table and runs the checks again.
then: Expects a helper file not to be found as a source file without a record, and a file that no record names, or that only a row for an unknown record names, to be found. Expects the package that holds the helper file to be found with the domain of the record that names the helper file and the domain of the other record. Expects the title of the record to be checked only against the record's own file, so an identifier that only the helper file declares is found missing. Without the helper_file table, expects every helper file to be found as a source file without a record, and no package of two domains.

title: Each whole service declaration in a user doc passes stego validate against the repository's registry
when: Reads each doc that the user doc inventory lists, writes each fenced YAML block whose first line is kind: service as the service.yaml of a new project with an empty fills folder, and runs the stego binary's validate there with STEGO_REGISTRY set to the repository's registry.
then: Expects stego validate to exit 0 for each block, and at least one such block, as README.md's quick start holds one.

title: STEGO's own tree holds the rule: each generated section of a user doc is what the spec gives
when: Runs assure.docSectionStale over STEGO's own source tree and the spec at the commit under test.
then: Expects no fault of the rule outside the committed list of known faults (ST-ASR-TOOL03) at the same commit, no listed fault of the rule that the tree no longer has, and no fault of the rule, by rule and key, in the list that the list at the base commit does not hold, the base being the commit ASSURE_RATCHET_BASE names or else the first parent, so the list only gets shorter until it is empty.
notes: With the flag -update-docs, the test first writes each generated section again in the working tree, from the working tree's spec, and logs each doc it wrote, to commit before the next run.

title: A change that alters or removes a CLI command a user doc names, and leaves the doc as it is, gives a reason; one that changes the doc gives none
when: Runs the check that the change gate runs (assure.docsLagChange) on a base whose README names one stego command in its prose and another only in a generated section, for a change that alters the descriptions of both, for one that removes the first, for one that also changes the README, and for one that alters no command.
then: Expects one reason for the altered command named in prose, which reads back as a fault of ST-STD-DOCS-R04 keyed by the command's record; one reason for the removed command; and no reason for the change that changes the README or for the change that alters no command.

title: No generator source imports a package for files, processes or the network, or calls an HTTP client or server
when: Parses every non-test Go file under internal/generator, and lists each import and each package-qualified name, through any import alias.
then: Expects no import of os, os/exec, os/signal, io/ioutil, syscall, net or plugin, and no use of an HTTP client, transport, server or file server.
notes: The generators use net/http only to check route patterns on an in-memory ServeMux, and net/url and net/textproto only to parse text, so those packages stay allowed.

title: No generator source reads the clock, a timer, the environment or a source of randomness
when: Parses every non-test Go file under internal/generator, as ST-STD-GEN-R01-T01 does.
then: Expects no use of time.Now, timers, context deadlines, os.Getenv and its kin, math/rand or crypto/rand. The test can list a known violation, and fails when a listed use is gone; the list is empty.
notes: The gRPC generator stopped proto compilation after 10 seconds until 2026-10-28. The timeout was removed, because the compiler's input size limits already bound the proto files.

title: Planning each built-in archetype ten times gives the same files in the same order
when: With a project for each built-in archetype: rest-crud, rpc-service and browser-service: Plans each project ten times in one process. Go starts each map iteration at a random place.
then: Expects every plan of a project to hold the same files, in the same order, with the same content.
notes: Not proof yet. The three archetypes reach 10 of the 26 components. These are not reached: cli-application, controller, go-sdk, grpc-application, http-application, kafka-producer, keycloak-provider, kubernetes-client, kubernetes-workload, outbox, postgres-client, rh-sso-auth, runtime-configuration, typescript-sdk, user-management and user-management-rhsso. A project for each of them, or a fixture context per generator, would make the test proof.

title: Every suite gives the same outcome on a workstation as in CI at one commit
when: Runs each suite command of the documented list on a developer's workstation, as an unprivileged user, in a network namespace whose only routes are loopback and the network of the local services that the suite starts, with KUBECONFIG unset, no kube configuration file, and no CI provider token, registry credential or cloud credential in the environment, at the commit under test, and reads the outcomes by test ID.
then: Expects each test ID that proves an obligation to have an outcome, and the same result (passed, failed or skipped) as the CI run of the same commit. Expects no test to be skipped or to fail because a cluster, a hosted service, a credential or a route out is missing, and names each test that is.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide: it runs every suite at once, so a suite that no domain owns, such as scripts or the Python suites, is also caught; the tests of ST-PAT-LOCAL-TEST-R01 run the same check one domain at a time. A missing outcome is a fault, not a pass. Compare with the CI outcomes of the same commit, so that a test that fails for its own assertion does not count against this rule.

title: Each test file belongs to one suite that one documented command runs
when: Reads the documented list of suite commands (the builder names the file and records it as tooling) and each test file that a test record names or that the config's test globs match (**/*_test.go, scripts/test_*.py).
then: Expects each suite in the list to have exactly one command, and each test file to belong to exactly one suite. Names each test file that no suite runs, and each suite with no command or with two.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide, so that a test file that no domain owns is also caught. Read the test globs from lathe.config.json, not from a copy, so a new kind of test file is also caught.

title: No obligation is proved only by a test that needs a real outside system
when: Reads the spec at the commit under test with the pinned Lathe and lists each test record that is external, or whose given, when, notes or test data set names an outside system: a hosted CI provider, Konflux, Argo CD, an OCI registry, an identity provider or a signer. For each, reads the other tests of the same obligation.
then: Expects each obligation that such a test proves to have at least one other test that runs against a local stand-in of that system, and names each obligation whose only tests need the real system.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. The stand-ins are a local OCI registry (the TLS registry fixture, scripts/registry-fixture.go), PostgreSQL in a local container, a fake of the hosted CI provider's API, Konflux and Argo CD that keeps their contract, a fixture signer that the test trusts in place of the provider's signer, and a kind cluster only where a real Kubernetes API is the thing under test.

title: Each local service that a suite starts is pinned by digest or by exact version and checksum
when: Scans every suite file, test helper, test data set and fixture script for each local service it starts: a container image, a downloaded binary, a Go SDK or a tool.
then: Expects each to be named by a sha256 digest, or by an exact version with a checksum that the suite checks before use, and to be started by the test or its suite. Names each that is named by a tag such as latest, by a version range, or with no checksum, and each that a test expects to be running already.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. A service that a test expects to find running, such as a database on a fixed port, is a fault even when it is pinned, because the suite does not start it.

title: A run of every suite leaves no file, container or process outside its temporary folder
when: Runs each suite command of the documented list with HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME and TMPDIR each set to a new empty folder, and XDG_CACHE_HOME set to the cache of pinned downloads. Lists the user's files, containers, volumes, networks and processes before and after the run.
then: Expects no file outside TMPDIR to be new or changed, apart from the outcomes file that the command names and new entries of the cache that are keyed by digest. Expects no container, volume, network or process that the run started to be left. Names each one that is.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. List the whole test folder, the user's containers (podman ps -a), volumes and networks, so that state left in an unexpected place is caught; ST-DLV-A4-SR01-T03 does the same for stego apply and stego delivery check.

title: Each obligation that a cluster or volume test proves also has a test that runs on a workstation
when: Reads the spec at the commit under test with the pinned Lathe and lists each obligation with its tests, and the size, level and notes of each test.
then: Expects each obligation with a test of size volume or worst case, or a test whose notes or test data set need a shared cluster, also to have a test that runs on a workstation. Names each obligation whose only proof needs a cluster.
notes: Not automated yet. Product-wide. AGENTS.md keeps performance and stress tests off the workstation, so this rule asks for a second test, not for a change of those tests.

title: No test record or measure expects debug-hatch output
when: Reads every test record, output contract and business outcome measure in data/ at the commit under test, and the observations.json and test files of the example services.
then: Expects no record about a generated service's signals whose expected result reads the output of log or log/slog or a line on standard error as its evidence, other than an expectation that standard error stays empty or that a text is absent, and no test file of an example service that asserts on standard error; the diagnostics of a command-line program, such as ST-SUP-RC04-OC30-T01, are not counted.
notes: Not automated yet: the probe runtime and its rules are not built yet. Planned file internal/assure/observability_standard_test.go. Owner decision of 2026-11-06: a declared domain probe is the only sanctioned path for a fill to emit logs or domain signals; log and log/slog stay allowed as a debug hatch only.

title: Every archetype of the common registry pins the one runtime module of the registry, at the checksum of its folder
when: Loads the common registry of the checkout, reads the module path of registry/runtime/go.mod, and computes the go.sum hash of the module zip of registry/runtime at the version that the archetypes pin.
then: Expects the module path github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime, the same pin in every archetype, with that module path and that hash, and a LICENSE in registry/runtime that is the repository's LICENSE. Expects a failure that names the new hash and the archetype files to change, when registry/runtime changes and the pin does not.
notes: Proved by TestRuntimeReleasedWithTheCommonRegistry; its subtest carries this ID. The tag registry/runtime/<version> at the same tree gives the same zip, because the module folder holds its own LICENSE: the Go module proxy adds the repository's LICENSE to a module in a subfolder that has none. So the pin is the checksum of the release, before and after the tag. A change of registry/runtime is a new runtime version: the archetypes then get a new runtime.version and runtime.sum, and a new archetype version (ST-SUP-INV10). Mutation check: the test fails when the sum of one archetype changes, or when a file of registry/runtime changes.

title: A generated service that imports a runtime package resolves the pin from the common registry with no network, builds with the pinned Go and runs
when: With a common registry in a temporary folder that holds a copy of registry/runtime and an archetype with the pin of the shipped archetypes, a service whose one component emits a background task that allocates 10.00 USD in three with github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/money is applied; module resolution (stego deps) runs with a private module cache and only local module proxies; the service is built with the pinned Go and the proxy off, and run; then it is built again with the work file of scripts/runtime-workspace.sh and an empty module cache, and run.
then: Expects go.mod to require only the pin, with no replace directive, go.sum to hold the pin's hash and the hash of its go.mod, no work file in the project and no drift. Expects each run to print allocated 334 USD 333 USD 333 USD and to stop cleanly on SIGTERM, and the workspace build to put no runtime version in the module cache.
notes: Proved by TestRuntimePinBuildsWithNoNetwork; its subtest carries this ID. It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test, and it fails on another version. Local stand-in (ST-STD-LOCAL): Generating stages the runtime folder of the common registry as a file module proxy when the folder's zip has the pinned hash, and puts it before the configured proxies; the test sets GOPROXY to that proxy and the download cache of the machine's module cache, then off, and the sum database off, so no command reaches github.com or any other host. The third-party modules that the runtime library requires must be in the machine's module cache, as they are after a test of registry/runtime. Before the first tag registry/runtime/<version> (ST-DIS-UC11-R06), stego build download cannot fetch the pin from the public proxy (see the builder notes).

title: Every runtime package takes the database/sql transaction and imports no driver
when: Reads the exported API of every package of the runtime module for parameters and fields that take a transaction, and the imports of every file that is not a test file.
then: Expects each such parameter or field to be *sql.Tx, an interface that *sql.Tx satisfies, or a type that an exported adapter builds from *sql.Tx, and no import of a database driver outside the test files.
notes: Planned as a check of the code-standard tests in internal/assure, beside the checks of ST-STD-RUNTIME-R01 and R02.

title: Only the connector package imports a driver, and the listener refuses a pooled DSN
when: Reads the imports of every non-test file of the runtime module, and opens the outbox Listener of the connector package with a DSN that names a transaction-mode pooler and with a direct DSN.
then: Expects a database driver imported only by files of github.com/jsell-rh/stego/registry/runtime/pgconn, the pooled DSN refused at start with an error that names the setting and no secret, and the direct DSN accepted.
notes: Planned as a check of the code-standard tests in internal/assure, beside ST-STD-RUNTIME-R06-T01, and a unit test in registry/runtime/pgconn/listen_test.go. Today the tenant package imports pgx outside its tests; the code change moves that code to pgconn. Review of PR #143 (outbox runtime).

title: The compiler contains a generator for every component the registry ships
when: Lists the components in registry/components and the generators the compiler build holds.
then: Expects each component to have a generator, and each generator to have a component.

title: Qualification fails when the signed artifact run holds a second artifact
when: Qualifies a release whose signed artifact run also holds a separate generator artifact.
then: Expects qualification to fail on an unknown artifact, so a release ships one compiler.

title: A component with no generator in the compiler build stops compilation before anything is written
when: Compiles a service whose component has no generator, a nil generator or a typed nil generator.
then: Expects a validation error and no plan, with no output, go.mod or .stego written; the compiler looks for no generator elsewhere.

title: No compiler source imports the plugin package
when: Parses the imports of every non-test Go source under cmd and internal, outside testdata.
then: Expects no import of Go's plugin package, so the compiler cannot load code at run time.
notes: This shows the compiler cannot load code. It does not show that the compiler downloads or runs no generator code by other means.
